title: Marguerite and the Typewriter
premise: In 1913 London, Petra Crane drives for the formidable suffragist Marguerite Ashworth, secretly reading every letter that passes through the house. When an abandoned child arrives with a note demanding her face be forgotten, Petra discovers the girl is tied to a smuggling ring moving fugitives out of England — one run by Marguerite's own brother, whose corruption has begun poisoning the cause itself. With only one berth left on the final boat to France and the police closing in, Petra must decide whether to save the child, expose the brother, or protect the woman she has come to love as family. She chooses all three at terrible cost: the child sails safely, the brother is exposed but escapes, and Petra — once a woman who kept busy hands and a low profile — takes Marguerite's hand publicly on the dock, claiming her place in a family not born but built.
about_author: S. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffragist correspondence in regional English collections. They write historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Letters I Wasn't Meant to Read
chapters.summary: Petra Crane's POV. We meet Petra as driver and silent reader of Marguerite Ashworth's mail, learning the household's rhythms and its fault lines — especially the charming brother, Edmund, whose donations never quite add up. A child appears on the doorstep at dawn clutching a note: forget this face. Petra hides her before Marguerite wakes. Emotional beat: wary tenderness cracking open a guarded heart.

chapters.title: One Berth, Two Names
chapters.summary: Alternating Petra and Marguerite POVs. The child, Nell, lets slip a name that connects Edmund to a network selling escape passages to hunted women — then pocketing the fees and reporting stragglers to police. Marguerite refuses to believe it; Petra finds the ledger proving it. The final boat leaves in six days with one berth unclaimed. Emotional beat: loyalty splitting down the middle as suspicion becomes certainty.

chapters.title: What the Brother Knew
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. Petra confronts Edmund privately; he offers her money and a berth of her own, revealing he knows she reads the letters — and that Marguerite's own arrest is already arranged. When Marguerite walks in on the bargain, the family fractures. Police arrive early; Petra burns the ledger copy, keeps the original, and puts Nell in the car. Emotional beat: betrayal weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, resolution. At the dock, Marguerite must choose between fleeing herself or giving Nell the berth; she gives it to the child, choosing found family over blood. Edmund slips away abroad, unpunished but exposed. Petra stays — not as staff, but as Marguerite's partner, their hands joined openly as the boat pulls out. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; a family chosen, not inherited.
